output.title: Cloudy apple juice bottling (1L glass bottles)

product.name: 1 litre cloudy apple juice bottle
product.description: One-litre glass bottle of cloudy apple juice, filled by nozzle, then capped with a red screw cap and wrapped with a paper label.

steps.name: Fill
steps.does: Fill each 1L bottle with cloudy apple juice through a nozzle (about 6 seconds per bottle filling).

steps.name: Cap
steps.does: Screw on the red cap to the filled bottle.

steps.name: Label
steps.does: Apply the paper label to the capped bottle.

steps.name: Inspect
steps.does: Use a camera to check fill level, cap presence/quality, and label presence/placement; reject bad bottles off the line.

output.quality: Camera inspection checks fill level, cap, and label; bottles that fail inspection are rejected and do not continue on the line.
constraints: Stainless steel frames for the line/handling area.
One bottle at a time (in sequence) on a belt conveyor.
Takt must support 240 bottles/hour with no station slower than the takt.
assumptions: A 1-shift calculation basis of 8 hours applies for converting the target rate to a line takt (rate itself is already in bottles/hour, so this mainly supports timing assumptions).
The screw-capping and labeling operations can be completed within the line takt, since only filling time (6 s) was explicitly given.
Reject handling routes bad bottles to a separate discard position (no rework).
The belt carries individual bottles without accumulating batches (no case/pallet level buffering described).

questions.question: 240 bottles/hour implies a takt of 15.0 s per bottle. You specified ~6 s filling, but what are the expected cycle times for capping and labeling (seconds each)?
questions.why: Station seconds must all fit within the 15.0 s takt; if cap/label are slower, the line design would need parallel heads or different cadence.

questions.question: For “bad bottles go off the line”, do you want rejection immediately at the inspection station (single-lane divert), or keep them on the belt for a downstream divert point?
questions.why: This affects layout and transport (diver timing, buffer space, and how the off-line chute/roller section is placed).

questions.question: Do bottles arrive already rinsed/sanitized and empty (with caps supplied separately), or does the line also need a bottle wash/sanitization and cap feeding step?
questions.why: If sanitization/cap supply is required, it adds discrete stations before Fill and changes what “off the line” means for bad units.
